# Import Capacity Table

This function requires the **Liquids** add-on.

A <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCTextPopup MCTextPopupHotSpot MCTextPopup_Open glossaryTerm MCTextPopupHotSpot_" alt="Closed" data-mc-alt2="Open">capacity table<span class="MCTextPopupBody popupBody"><span class="MCTextPopupArrow"></span>A table showing the capacities or volumes of a tank for various liquid levels measured from the reference gauge point; also known as a strapping table, tank capacity table or calibration table.</span></a> (strapping table) can be manually entered from the Tank Editor or imported from a tab-delimited file available from <a href="mailto:flowcal.support@quorumsoftware.com" class="InlineLink">Customer Support</a>.

The import process supports import of a single or multiple tanks, and a single capacity table or multiple tables in the same file.

Each capacity table belongs to a specified tank and is <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCTextPopup MCTextPopupHotSpot MCTextPopup_Open glossaryTerm MCTextPopupHotSpot_" alt="Closed" data-mc-alt2="Open">datetime effective<span class="MCTextPopupBody popupBody"><span class="MCTextPopupArrow"></span>Datetime effective records have a defined start date and time and a defined end date and time.</span></a>. Capacity tables are identified by name, and a tank may have more than one capacity table. Reasons for having multiple capacity tables include separate tables for high-leg and low-leg roof configurations, and alternate tables that depend on product density.

FLOWCAL does not automatically switch between available capacity tables. Users must manually maintain the active table via the [Tank Editor Characteristics tab](../Tank%20Editor/Configuration/Tank%20Editor_Config%20-%20Characteristics%20Tab.md).

Tanks are not auto-created during the capacity table import process, so the tank associated with the table must exist in FLOWCAL prior to importing a file.

<div class="procedure">

To import a capacity table:

1.  Go to **Import** \> **Capacity Table**.

2.  Click the browse button next to the **Import File** field to select the text file to import, or type the file path into the field.

    

<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 541;height: 185;" />

3.  Click the **Import** button. A dialog box will display, providing information about the import.

4.  When the import is complete, go to **Setup** \> **Tank Editor** \> **Tools** \> **Capacity Table** to view the imported data.

</div>

If capacity tables already exist for a tank, they will be split as needed to account for the date and time of the imported tables. If the date and time of an imported table encompass existing gauge tickets and tank run tickets, these tickets will not be automatically recalculated. Each ticket will need to be manually edited and confirmed when the import is complete and validations have been performed.

A capacity table can be entered or imported manually. The file import service does not support the import of capacity tables.

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Capacity Table File Format">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Capacity Table File Format</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Capacity Table File Format">

Contact <a href="mailto:flowcal.support@quorumsoftware.com" class="notelink">Customer Support</a> to obtain the Capacity Table file format.

The following is additional information regarding the import of capacity tables:

- When importing a capacity table for a tank, the first record must be a header row, followed by the table rows for the tank. If there is no header record, the capacity table will not import. Header records contain general information about the capacity table.
- After the header record, any number of table records can be imported. Table records contain tank levels and volumes. Each table record must have a level and either the volume at the given level, or the volume per increment and the number of increments per zone. If a record has incomplete parameters, an error message will be generated.
- If values for **Total Volume for the Tank at Specified Tank Level** and **Volume per Increment for the Zone/Increments in the Zone** are imported, the imported volume at level will be validated against the calculated volume at that level, based on the incremental volumes. If a record has inconsistent volumes, an error message will be generated.
- A shell temperature correction must be applied to all tanks with volumes greater than 5,000 bbl. If the total calculated volume for the tank exceeds 5,000 barrels, the **Apply Shell Temperature Correction, CTSh** field in the Capacity Table Setup screen will automatically be set to "true" regardless of the original import value.

</div>

Windows has a hard-coded limit of 260 characters for file paths; file paths longer than this will not work. Importing files from a local install allows for using drive letters for network file paths; however, Citrix resolves the actual network location, which can cause the number of characters in a file path to exceed this limit.
